messages.subject: Re: install.package("rJava") fails
messages.body_plain:
Dear Carl,

sorry I wasn't able to respond on time. Actually I tried to compile again, but I got similar errors, so I was a bit perplexed.

I just did a fresh check out from the repository and tried again. The result is, for rho fails to localize clang during configuration, even though llvm and clang binaries are definitely in the PATH. From the configuration, I get the warning

configure: WARNING: "clang compiler needed for llvm-jit"

and in the end

Options not enabled: memory profiling, LLVM JIT compiler

My platform is Ubuntu 14.04 (trusty), running on a VirtualBox VM.

I wonder how the existence of llvm is checked and if it is necessary to tell explicitly not to use the installed gcc compliler (?).

The commands I am using are the following:

tools/rsync-recommended
./configure --enable-llvm-jit --enable-maintainer-mode
make
make check

> rho should now compile for clang + llvm 3.5, 3.6 and 3.8 (and probably 3.4, but I haven't tested it recently) and gcc 4.9 and 5.0.  When compiled under gcc, the llvm JIT is automatically disabled.

messages.subject: Re: install.package("rJava") fails
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the bug report.

I've just pushed a change that makes the configure script prefer clang over other compilers if it's available, which should fix this issue as long as clang and clang++ are in the PATH.

Also, if needed, you can explicitly specify the compilers to use by setting the CC and CXX environment variables when running configure.
  e.g.  CC=/usr/local/bin/clang CXX=/usr/local/bin/clang++ ./configure
You can get a list of configuration options by passing '--help' to the configure script.

Please let me know if you run into any other issues.

Thanks,
Karl
